title: engineering-all-hands-2026-05-13
content:
Engineering All-Hands — 2026-05-13

Owner: Priya Desai (platform-engineering)
Attendees (notes): entire Eng org + invited PM/product reps; summary below for folks who couldn't make it.

Purpose / TL;DR:
- Quick status on production health, reliability work, and upcoming rollouts.
- Highlights from serving-runtime, observability, and private-deploy teams.
- Action items and follow-ups for the next two weeks.

1) Company / org context
- Brief from product: Dedicated & Private shipments are driving new enterprise discussions. Growth signal: 3 active Dedicated trials in EMEA started this quarter.
- Finance check-in: footprint expansion is OK provided we keep unit cost under control — optimization work (Optimize team) will be increasingly important.

2) Production health snapshot (past 7 days)
- Availability: 99.94% across hosted regions (measured per service). No customer-facing downtime.
- Incident summary: One elevated incident on 2026-05-09 (JIRA-ENG-4821) caused degraded throughput for a subset of Dedicated pool customers for ~45 minutes during a control-plane database failover. Root cause: race condition during connection rehydration in the routing service.
  - Mitigation: rollback to stable routing proxy (hotfix rolled by release-eng at 09:42 UTC). Full mitigation patch merged (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2147).
  - Action items: add 1) better connection backoff in router (owner: Miles), 2) automated failover test to run in staging (owner: SRE).
- Latency: p50 token-gen latency (hosted) = 18ms, p95 = 140ms, p99 = 380ms. Slight uptick in p99 vs last month due to higher long-context requests from a single enterprise customer; we have a mitigation plan (prefix caching + kv cache evictions) rolling out next week.

3) Serving-runtime highlights
- Quantization v2 rollout: Prod canaries started 05/11 for small-medium Llama variants. Early metrics show ~1.6x throughput improvement and ~25% GPU memory reduction for quantized runs. Still monitoring for small regressions in rare tokens; research is pairing with QA to extend evals.
- Kernel selection improvements: new heuristic added to pick fused attention kernels for <2048 seq-length; expected to reduce p50 by ~5-10% for mid-length workloads.
- Continuous batching: tuning landing later this sprint—will enable higher throughput for high-concurrency endpoints without impacting p50.

4) Observability & Console
- Token-level cost breakdown shipped to staging console this week. This gives teams real-time per-route token cost and should help product teams debug cost spikes. (Owner: Samira)
- New tracing hook for canary rollouts: can now surface model variant traces by rollout ID in the trace view.
- Roadblocks: retention infra needs budget approval to move to 90d trace retention; finance + product need to sign off.

5) Private deployments & security
- Private control plane alpha completed with one pilot customer. On-prem installer (air-gapped) passed initial compliance tests.
- Key management integration: early KMS plugin prototype works with AWS KMS & Hashicorp Vault (PR Q3 planning).

6) Platform & infra
- Autoscale policy improvements: new predictive-scaling model using time-series forecasts to prepare Dedicated pools before traffic spikes. Early results show ~12% fewer cold-starts in tests. (Owner: Jorge)
- Storage: migrated metrics ingestion to a partitioned store; long-term disk growth controlled.

7) Release cadence & upcoming rollouts
- Next week (week of 05/18): Canary rollout of quantization v2 to 15% of traffic for approved models. Watchlist: p95/p99 latency, hallucination regression tests.
- 05/22: Observability token-cost dashboard to go live for internal customer success testing.
- End of May: Private control plane beta (3 pilot customers) — we need final security sign-off and a short runbook for on-prem installs.

8) Hiring & org updates
- New hires: welcome to two new SREs (Talia Green, Viktor Kuznetsov) and an infra SWE (Yara Ali) joining platform-engineering this month.
- Open roles: infra reliability, infra infra-ops (2), applied-ml inference engineer (1). Please refer candidates to people-ops; referral bonus applies.

9) Shoutouts
- Shoutout to Release Eng and SRE for the incident fast rollback and clean postmortem.
- Shoutout to Research & QA for running extended evals on quantization v2 overnight.

10) Questions & answers (selected)
- Q: What happens if quantization causes downstream quality regressions?
  A: Canary gates include eval suites and production synthetic prompts; we have auto-fallback to float32 variants and will pause rollouts if regression > configured threshold.
- Q: Can product teams opt-out of auto-batching?
  A: Yes, per-route controls are available in the console; opt-out is intended for ultra-low-latency single-token scenarios.

11) Open action items (owners & due dates)
- Miles: implement router connection backoff + unit tests — due 2026-05-20.
- SRE (oncall): add automated DB failover test in staging — due 2026-05-18.
- Samira: enable 30-day internal retention expansion in staging and collect perf impact — due 2026-05-19.
- Jorge: complete predictive-scaler rollout plan & runbook — due 2026-05-25.
- Research/QA: extend eval corpus to include customer long-context prompts (add 5k prompts) — due 2026-05-26.

12) Notes to self / informal
- Need to sync with Sales on Dedicated trials to align expected capacity increases.
- Follow up with Legal for on-prem compliance checklist — ask for template next week.

Attachments & links (in meeting notes):
- Incident postmortem draft: JIRA-ENG-4821
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2147
- Canary rollout doc: confluence.redwood.internal/ENG-Platform/CanaryRollouts

If you want edits to the action item owners or to the rollout windows, drop a note in #eng-platform or file a comment on the Confluence doc.

— End of notes —

(These notes are a working draft — will publish final version to Confluence after action-item updates and PM sign-off.)
